lines.t: Down at Sunny Pines on Sunday noon,
The breeze was hummin’ an old hymn tune.
Old Earl revved up with a toothpick grin,
Said, “Let’s see who’s fastest — loser cleans the muffin tin!”
Gladys lined up, hair done tight,
Glasses on crooked, said, “Honey, hold my Sprite!”
Good ol’ Bob stood by with fries in hand,
Said, “Run this race like the good Lord planned!”
They’re rollin’ strong in electric grace,
Buzzin’ wheels in the Great Wheelchair Race.
Through pain and laughter, wrinkles and cheer,
They’re finishin’ strong in top‑speed gear.
Some folks run, some folks crawl,
But these folks scoot — surrenderin’ all.
‘Cause the one who endures through the pain,
And perseveres, is the one who finishes the race — Amen!
Mabel hit turbo, yelled, “Eat my dust!”
Earl said, “Slow down, your hubcap’s rust!”
Wheels were whirrin’, hearts were wild,
Half the crowd hadn’t moved that fast in a while.
Gladys took the shortcut ‘round the shed,
Clipped a bush, lost her bread.
But she laughed so hard, she hollered out,
“Maybe Heaven’ll have smoother routes!”
They’re rollin’ strong in electric grace,
Buzzin’ wheels in the Great Wheelchair Race.
Through pain and laughter, wrinkles and cheer,
They’re finishin’ strong in top‑speed gear.
Some folks run, some folks crawl,
But these folks scoot — surrenderin’ all.
‘Cause the one who endures through the pain,
And perseveres, is the one who finishes the race — Amen!
At the finish line, they slowed their roll,
Smiles and stories fed every soul.
Good ol’ Bob said, “We’ve all won today —
Endured the bumps and found our way.”
Mabel raised her hands to Heaven’s door,
Said, “I’ll race again when I get restored!”
They’re rollin’ home in electric grace,
Joyous hearts in the slow‑mo chase.
Wheels may stop, but faith won’t tire,
Old souls lifted, full of fire!
For the one who trusts when life gets tough,
Will soar beyond when the road gets rough.
From Sunny Pines to the skies above,
They’ll fly — with eagle’s wings of love.
